 The Role: 
This position is a strategic consulting role responsible for providing professional risk consulting and risk solutions aimed at supporting the sound operations and strategic development of organizations. The incumbent will be required to identify, assess, and address various complex risks arising from both internal and external business environments, including policy risks, market risks, compliance risks, and operational risks.

 Candidates are required to possess more than five years of in-depth policy analysis experience. The role focuses on forward-looking risk forecasting by systematically analyzing government policy announcements, international geopolitical events, and industry statistical data. The consultant must accurately identify potential emerging risks and external uncertainties in advance, formulate targeted and executable risk response strategies, and provide professional solution recommendations to prevent and reduce organizational risk losses.

 Key Responsibilities： 

- Conduct in-depth research on topics such as the macroeconomic environment, regional development, industry trends, the international landscape, and public governance; independently carry out data collection, information organization, data analysis, and the distillation of key insights.

- Responsible for providing professional risk consulting and risk solutions designed to support the sound operations and strategic development of various organizations. The incumbent must identify, assess, and address a wide range of complex risks arising from both internal and external business environments, including policy risks, market risks, compliance risks, and operational risks.

- Continuously monitor cutting-edge industry developments, policy trends, and changes in the external environment, and regularly publish various thematic research reports and trend analysis reports.

 You idealy have: 

- Bachelor's degree or higher; at least 3 years of work experience in research and analysis.

- Possesses strong writing skills, including excellent written expression, logical reasoning, and structured writing abilities, and is capable of producing in-depth research reports.

- By searching, screening, and synthesizing information from publicly available online sources, we extract valuable leads from the vast amount of publicly available internet information and compile them into reports.

- Diligent and responsible, able to submit reports promptly and efficiently in accordance with company requirements.

 Salary: 

 We use a project-based billing system, with compensation for each report ranging from $500 to $1,000. The specific amount is determined based on a combination of factors, including the report’s complexity, comprehensiveness, and quality.

 Please be sure to include your most recent resume when you drop off your application so that we can conduct a comprehensive evaluation of you.

 To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/felyri-consulting-limited-research-consultant

 We are looking for translators with experience in translating patents from English into Portuguese (Brazil) (native-level fluency of Portuguese) with immediate availability for a patent translation project.

- Proficiency in using CAT tools like XTM for project management and quality assessment.

 Compensation

About us 
 At Pencil, we are driving innovation in advertising technology through our state-of-the-art SaaS product, which harnesses Agentic AI to redefine content creation. Our mission is to make AI the default in advertising without replacing creative people. To achieve this, we need to make sure that our technology isn't just in the hands of big brands - we need to try to help small businesses and creative individuals too.

 The role 
 Workflows are how most of the creative on Pencil gets made. A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

 You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

 You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

 Key responsibilities 

- Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

- Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

- Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

- Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

- Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

- Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

- Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

- Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

- Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

- Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

- Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

- Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

 As a Market Curation Editor for Sports, you'll support the Product Data Operations team supporting a new social-predictions app moving through a beta launch. An automated pipeline drafts candidate prediction markets every night; you are the human judgment layer on top of it — deciding which go live, sharpening the ones that are nearly right, and catching the markets the pipeline missed entirely. This role calls for deep, current expertise in professional and collegiate sport and in the rule conventions that govern how results are officially determined.
 What You'll Do 

- Review a daily queue of system-generated sports markets against a fixed completion deadline, working event by event across every market a fixture generates.

- Assess each candidate market for factual accuracy, clarity, and whether the resolution criteria can actually be adjudicated against a named authoritative source and a defined settlement date.

- Verify that open and close timing is correct for the underlying event, including scheduled and unscheduled delays.

- Apply the correct settlement convention for the league in question — overtime, shootouts, postponement and abandonment, minimum-play thresholds on player props, and official statistical corrections.

- Confirm policy fit against community standards and content guidelines, escalating anything ambiguous or sensitive rather than making an unsupported call.

- Approve, edit, or reject each candidate, recording a structured reason every time — this record is a product deliverable, not admin.

- Rewrite questions and resolution language for precision, and for how fans actually talk about the event.

- Author timestamped clarifications when ambiguity emerges in a live market, and resolve settlement exceptions the data feed can't handle.

- Run proactive gap scans — monitor live markets for visible errors, and track schedules, team news, and social platforms for events the pipeline didn't capture.

- Participate in weekly calibration reviews to stay consistent with published guidelines and fellow curators.

 What We're Looking For 

- 3+ years in sports trading, sports data operations, sports journalism or editorial, or a comparable role requiring current subject-matter expertise.

- Demonstrable current fluency in sport — following it now, not historically — across professional and collegiate leagues in major sports.

- Fluency with sports culture and sports social media (trades, free agency, breaking news accounts).

- Working knowledge of official rule and settlement conventions for major leagues, and of which sources are authoritative for results and statistics.

- Proven judgment on edge cases: suspended and abandoned events, statistical corrections, contested outcomes, ambiguous official rulings.

- Ability to interpret official sources quickly and reach a defensible determination.

- Exceptional written precision under deadline — able to write unambiguous rules that hold up after the outcome is known.

- Comfort applying a written policy framework, with the instinct to escalate rather than guess.

- Flexible availability for evening, overnight, and weekend work as needed around live events.

 Nice to Have 

- Experience trading on, or working with, prediction markets, sportsbooks, exchanges, or DFS platforms.

- Prior work on a trading desk, or standing as a super-user of prediction apps.

- Familiarity with content policy, moderation frameworks, or editorial standards.

 How We'll Measure Success 

- Consistent completion of the daily queue against the hard deadline.

- Decision quality — agreement with peers and the lead on calibration samples, and a low rate of published markets requiring void, amendment, or resettlement.

- Reason quality — structured rejection reasons that are specific and correctly categorized.

- Rewrite quality — published questions that survive contact with the outcome without dispute.

- Proactive contribution — relevant events and markets you surface that the pipeline didn't generate.

 Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand.
 We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents.

- Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation.

- Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts.

- Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.

- Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems.

- An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate.

- High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes.

- Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones.

- Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production.

- Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above.

 Why This Role Matters for You

- Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets.

- Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need.

 At Cloudbeds , we're not just building software, we're transforming hospitality. Our platform powers hotels across 150 countries, processing billions in bookings annually. From boutique properties to large hotel groups, we help hoteliers transform operations and uplevel their commercial strategy through a unified platform that integrates with hundreds of partners.  How You'll Make an Impact: 

 As our Customer Support Coach – Integrations in Thailand, you’ll be the deepest expert at Cloudbeds on our MecX Tech integrations, principally the Carmen Accounting interface and the TM30 Immigration reporting integration. You’ll be the person Thai customers, support agents, and partners turn to when something isn’t flowing. Thai hoteliers must report every foreign guest to Immigration within 24 hours under TM30, and every night’s revenue has to land cleanly in a finance system built for Thai accounting standards. When those handoffs break, front desk teams become data-entry clerks and properties carry real regulatory risk.

 This is a coaching role as much as a technical one. You’ll resolve the hardest escalations yourself, then turn each one into playbooks, articles, and hands-on training that raise the floor for the whole support org, and you’ll use AI and automation to cut repetitive diagnostic work so your time goes to the hoteliers who need it. If you get satisfaction from finding the root cause, fixing it for good, and teaching others to spot it, we’d love to hear from you.

 Our Customer Support Team: 

 We are a fully remote group of former hoteliers, technologists, and customer experience professionals focused on removing unnecessary manual work so we can spend more time solving the problem behind the problem and helping customers feel confident and supported. If you’re driven by curiosity and ownership and prefer deeply personalized hospitality moments over repetitive operational tasks, you’ll feel right at home here.

 What You Bring to the Team: 

- Serve as the subject matter expert and primary escalation point for MecX Tech integrations, with end-to-end ownership of the Carmen Accounting interface and the TM30 Immigration reporting integration. Investigate complex failures using logs, API tooling, and structured troubleshooting until you reach the root cause, not just a workaround.

- Make sure Thai properties meet their TM30 obligations reliably through Cloudbeds by tracking submission success rates and driving down failures before they become regulatory exposure. Partner with Onboarding and Sales so new properties are configured correctly on Carmen and TM30 from day one.

- Translate recurring field issues into clear, well-evidenced bug reports and product feedback, advocate for the Thai market internally, and track fixes through to release.

- Own the knowledge base, capturing what you learn in searchable, reusable documentation in both Thai and English so the next person doesn’t have to solve it again.

- Track and report integration health metrics (ticket volume, time to resolution, escalation rate, integration error rates, and more), and use them to target where coaching and product fixes will have the most impact.

 What Sets You Up for Success: 

- 3+ years in a technical support, integrations support, or implementation role, able to read API documentation, interpret JSON/XML payloads, work through logs, and use tools like Postman to isolate where a data flow breaks

- Experience in hotel operations or hospitality technology (PMS, channel manager, POS, or hotel back-office/accounting systems), familiar with night audit, revenue posting, and how a hotel closes its day

- Proven ability to teach, mentor, and level up peers: you document as you go and get satisfaction from making yourself unnecessar

About Us: 

 Spreedly is the Intelligent Payments Platform for businesses that want to own their payments strategy. Founded in 2007 and headquartered in Durham, NC, we give merchants, platforms, and fintechs a single API to connect to 150+ payment gateways and 40+ payment methods across 100+ countries, along with the intelligence to decide where every transaction should go. We're vendor-agnostic by design. Our customers choose their providers, keep their payment data portable, and never have to rebuild their stack to adopt something new.

 Payments are getting more complex, not less. Every new market, payment method, fraud tool, and now every AI agent checking out on a shopper's behalf adds another integration and another decision. Spreedly turns that complexity into an advantage. Our PCI Level 1 vault keeps cards and network tokens portable across providers. Smart routing and retries recover revenue lost to avoidable declines. Fraud and 3DS tools plug in with a single API call. And our payments intelligence turns transaction data into decisions merchants can act on. As agentic commerce moves from experiment to real sales channel, we're building the infrastructure that lets merchants accept agent-initiated payments through the providers they already trust.

 For the people who work here, that means hard technical problems at real scale, billions of dollars in annual transactions, at a moment when the rules of commerce are being rewritten. If you want ownership and work that shows up directly in your customers' revenue, you'll fit right in.

 About the Role 

 Spreedly is looking for a Support Engineer to take on our most complex customer issues and bridge the gap between support and engineering. You'll go beyond identifying a bug: you'll investigate where it occurs, explain its impact, and give engineering the evidence and technical context needed to resolve it.

 You'll join an international support team that serves customers, partners, prospects, and internal colleagues. Our Tier 1 team provides round-the-clock support, while Tier 2 handles deeper technical investigations. This role brings additional engineering depth to that work, particularly in troubleshooting SDKs and complex payments integrations.

 This is a hands-on, player-coach role. You'll work directly on difficult cases while helping teammates develop their technical skills. We also want this hire to help lay the foundation for a potential Tier 3 support function. That expansion and any future team leadership role are subject to leadership approval, rather than guaranteed next steps.

 We expect roughly 60% of your time to focus on complex customer tickets, most of them from our top-tier accounts. The remaining time will involve retrospectives, customer advocacy, cross-functional projects, and coaching.

 Responsibilities

- 
 Own complex technical investigations, particularly for our top-tier customer accounts. Read and navigate source code, analyze logs, and inspect API and SDK behavior to pinpoint issues.

- 
 Reproduce customer issues in test environments so findings are confirmed before they reach engineering.

- 
 Build clear, actionable engineering escalations that explain the problem, where it occurs, and potential approaches to resolving it, with engineering retaining final decisions on changes.

- 
 Bring SDK troubleshooting expertise to support for our Checkout SDK and share that knowledge across the team in collaboration with engineering.

- 
 Help manage incidents and keep customers informed, translating technical findings into clear explanations and advocating for their needs across departments.

- 
 Identify recurring patterns across cases, lead retrospectives, and turn findings into improvements that prevent repeat issues and reduce prolonged back-and-forth with engineering.

- 
 Improve documentation, share investigation techniques, and coach support teammates through unfamiliar technical problems.

- 
 Take ownership of cross-functional projects, from defining the problem through completing and rolling out the work.

- 

 Candidate Requirements

- 
 A foundation in software development through professional experience, coding education, or another hands-on path, with the ability to investigate code and explain technical findings.

- 
 Experience troubleshooting SDKs and working with APIs, including understanding how integrations behave in a web environment.

- 
 Customer-facing technical experience and the ability to communicate clearly with customers during complex or prolonged investigations.

- 
 The ability to coach others and lead work without formal authority. You don't need a previous management title, but you should be able to guide teammates and collaborate effectively with engineering.

- 
 Independent problem-solving and project ownership: you can work through ambiguity, move an investigation forward, and know when to bring others in.

- 
 Payments experience is strongly preferred because it will help you ramp quick

We are looking for a proactive and detail-oriented CEO Office Associate with strong operational drive who wants to play a vital role in enabling our mission on climate solutions.

This role serves as the logistical and administrative backbone of the CEO Office, focusing on complex end-to-end international travel, administrative operations, expense management, and executive hospitality. Working across multiple time zones, the CEO Office Associate will also play a key role in building and polishing executive presentations, slide decks, and meeting collateral, while providing seamless calendar backup when needed.

The CEO and Chief of Staff operate in a fast-paced global environment. This position requires meticulous precision, sound operational judgement, high discretion, and the confidence to take ownership of tasks to keep our leadership team running smoothly. Reporting to the CEO Office Operations Manager, this role requires close collaboration with colleagues and stakeholder EAs across geographies, strong communication skills, and the ability to adapt quickly to shifting priorities. 

 If you excel at creating structure amid constant change, enjoy problem-solving, and take satisfaction in making complex logistics run smoothly, while helping drive meaningful change, we’d love for you to apply.

 Inbox Operations & Diary Continuity (Support & Back-up)

 Administrative Inbox Triaging: Monitor the CEO Office inbox for administrative confirmations, receipts, vendor communications, and routine inquiries

- 
 Participate in a weekly diary review and look-ahead session to anticipate upcoming needs and manage last-minute changes

- 
 Business Continuity & Absence Coverage : Provide complete diary coverage in the absence of the Senior Executive Assistant and during peak workload periods managing real-time schedule shifts and urgent calendar requests under the guidance of the CEO Office Operations Manager

 Travel and Logistics for CEO & Chief Of Staff 

- End-to-End Travel Booking: Execute comprehensive international travel bookings (flights, rail, hotels, ground transport)

- Track travel plans across the year to identify opportunities for stakeholder meetings or events while the CEO and or the Chief of Staff are in-country

- Administrative Travel Requirements: Fully own visa applications, passport renewals, travel insurance, vaccination requirements, and destination logistics

- Ensure the knowledge-management of all of the above is sound so the Operations manager, the Chief of Staff and the CEO know where to find what they need while travelling

 Meeting Logistics, Materials & Executive Hospitality 

- 
 Presentations, Decks & Materials Support: Format and polish presentations, handouts, and meeting collateral for executive reviews, team updates, and leadership meetings

- 
 Meeting Setup & Hospitality: Book internal & external meeting rooms, arrange catering, coordinate AV/tech setup

- 
 Meeting Pack Distribution: Ensure all completed briefing materials, agendas, and presentation collateral are formatted, circulated, and ready in advance

 Administration, Coordination and Ad Hoc Support 

- Manage expenses for the CEO and Chief of Staff, including collating, verifying, and uploading receipts to the expense system

- Support invoice processing, budget tracking, and accurate record-keeping

- Maintain and support the optimization of the CEO Office Google Drive file management system, ensuring structured organization, naming conventions, and secure access control

- Work closely with the CEO Office Operations Manager and Senior Executive Assistant to ensure alignment and consistency across the CEO Office

- Provide administrative and logistical support for internal projects and events

- Undertake other reasonable duties as requested by the CEO Office Operations Manager

 Our ideal candidate has

- Relevant work experience as an Executive Assistant or experience in a similar position working for a busy principal, with a proven track record of autonomously managing a complicated schedule, with upward management skills developed in a fast-paced, global, impact-driven environment.

- Proven ability to manage complex schedules autonomously, exercise sound judgement, and influence upwards with confidence and tact.

- High level of discretion, professionalism, and reliability when handling sensitive information.

Floowi connects top LATAM professionals with leading U.S. companies through remote talent solutions. Our mission is to make LATAM the world’s premier hub for growth and excellence.
 🌟 About our Client: A fast-growing direct-to-consumer beauty company that develops and sells hair care and styling products through its own e-commerce sites and major online marketplaces. The company runs high-volume digital operations with in-house brand, creative, and site experience teams.
 ✍ Short Description: You will own the execution of the company’s email and SMS retention program, building and optimizing the customer journeys that turn first-time buyers into loyal customers. Day to day, you will build and deploy promotional campaigns and automated flows, segment audiences, run A/B tests, and manage QA before every send. You will analyze performance and turn insights into a clear testing roadmap. You will also support retention initiatives beyond email, including loyalty, subscriptions, and direct mail, working closely with the brand and creative teams.
 🌎 Location: 100% Remote (LATAM only)
 🗣 Language Requirements: Advanced English (C1+)
 ⏰ Schedule: Full-time, aligned with EST
 😀 Start Date: ASAP
 💰 Compensation & Benefits:

- Competitive salary in USD

- Remote-first flexibility. Work from anywhere.

 💼 Responsibilities:

- Build, target, and deploy promotional and automated email and SMS campaigns end to end, from concept to send

- Develop, manage, and optimize lifecycle journeys such as welcome, post-purchase, replenishment, abandonment, and winback

- Improve segmentation and personalization to increase repeat purchases and customer lifetime value (LTV)

- Monitor open rates, CTR, conversion, and LTV, and run a structured A/B testing roadmap based on the results

- Support retention programs across loyalty, subscriptions, direct mail, and SMS, keeping every channel cohesive

- Partner with the brand and creative teams on new campaign ideas aligned with industry trends

- Lead QA on every campaign and ensure compliance with email and SMS marketing regulations

 💡 Qualifications:

- Bachelor’s degree

- 4+ years of experience in retention, lifecycle, or CRM marketing, ideally in ecommerce or DTC

- Hands-on experience building and optimizing lifecycle flows (welcome, post-purchase, replenishment, winback, abandonment)

- Experience with ESP and SMS platforms; Klaviyo strongly preferred

- Experience with subscription and/or loyalty programs for high-volume DTC brands

- Strong skills in campaign analysis, A/B testing, and performance measurement

- Strong project management skills and comfort working cross-functionally

 📩 If you meet the experience outlined above, we’d love to hear from you. Please apply, our team is excited about your application and will be in touch as soon as possible.

At Montu UK , we are passionate about improving the lives of patients who have often exhausted conventional treatment options. Through our Alternaleaf clinic, we are helping people living with chronic and debilitating conditions access treatments that can make a genuine difference to their quality of life.

 We are looking for Consultant Anaesthetists who are interested in exploring the growing field of medical cannabis and developing their expertise in chronic pain management.

 This is an exciting opportunity to be part of a rapidly growing healthcare organisation, working alongside a multidisciplinary team of experienced clinicians who share a passion for improving patient outcomes.

 With a fully funded Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management and comprehensive specialist training, we are keen to hear from consultants who are open to exploring new approaches to patient care and want to make a meaningful difference in an evolving area of medicine.

 Previous chronic pain experience is not essential. What matters is a genuine interest in learning, an open-minded approach to alternative treatment options and a commitment to delivering excellent patient care.

 What is the job?

 As a Consultant Anaesthetist at Montu, the role focuses on assessing and supporting patients living with chronic pain who may have exhausted conventional treatment options.

 Working within our Alternaleaf clinic, consultants play a central role in determining the suitability of cannabis-based prescription medicines (CBPMs), developing individualised treatment plans and supporting patients throughout their treatment journey.

 The position offers the opportunity to build on existing expertise in analgesic pharmacology, pain management and opioid stewardship while developing specialist knowledge in an evolving area of medicine.

 Our multidisciplinary approach brings together consultants, nurses, pharmacists and other healthcare professionals, allowing consultants to focus on clinical assessment, prescribing decisions and ongoing patient care.

 Sponsored Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management

 As part of our commitment to clinical development, Montu is offering a fully funded Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management through the University of South Wales , delivered fully online in partnership with Learna.

 The programme provides an opportunity to develop specialist knowledge in chronic pain management while continuing to gain practical clinical experience within our multidisciplinary team.

 About the diploma 

- 
 A 12-month, part-time postgraduate diploma with all teaching and assessment completed online.

- 
 Focuses on interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary pain management, assessment and service provision.

- 
 Full course fees funded by Montu UK.

- 
 Two hours of protected, paid study time each week.

 Further information about the programme is available through the University of South Wales .

 Eligibility 

- 
 A minimum working commitment of 24 hours per week with Montu.

- 
 Two of those hours each week are allocated as protected, paid study time.

- 
 Continued employment with Montu at a minimum of 24 hours per week for the duration of the diploma.

 What will you be doing?

- 
 Providing high-quality care for patients seeking medical cannabis treatment for chronic pain and other qualifying conditions.

- 
 Conducting patient consultations, including clinical assessments, prescribing decisions and ongoing patient management.

- 
 Applying anaesthetic expertise in analgesic pharmacology, drug interactions and opioid stewardship to support safe prescribing.

- 
 Reviewing patient progress and treatment effectiveness, making adjustments where clinically appropriate.

- 
 Engaging in clinical outcome data collection to support evidence-based practice.

- 
 Contributing to clinical governance and maintaining robust patient care standards.

- 
 Collaborating with a multidisciplinary team, including nurses and pharmacists.

- 
 Completing the sponsored Postgraduate Diploma in Pain Management alongside clinical responsibilities.

- 
 Participating in ongoing training and professional development, including specialist training in cannabis-based prescription medicines.

 What you need

- 
 Full GMC registration with a current licence to practise.

- 
 Completion of specialist training in Anaesthesia (CCT/CCST) or equivalent.

- 
 Entry on the GMC Specialist Register for Anaesthesia.

- 
 Strong knowledge of analgesic pharmacology, pain management and safe prescribing.

- 
 Excellent communication skills and a patient-centred approach to care.

- 
 Ability to work independently while contributing to a multidisciplinary clinical team.

- 
 A strong interest in chronic pain and alternative treatment options.

- 
 Willingness to participate in clinical outcome data collection and reporting.

- 
 Ability to commit to a minimum of 24 hours per week for the duration of the diploma.

I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

 I started Anima to change that.

 Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

 We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

 Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. 

 If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

 -- Shun

 £25k–£75k base, depending on location and experience, plus equity 
 Remote, UK time zone 

 The role

 When a clinic gets stuck, you’ll help them move forward. You’ll become an expert in Anima, untangle technical problems and give clinicians and practice teams clear, practical answers.

 This is a hands-on IC role with real ownership of how support develops at Anima. You’ll resolve customer issues while helping build the function: deciding what to measure, improving how the team works and shaping what excellent support looks like as we scale.

 What you’ll do

- 
 Own issues through to resolution. Support customers through Intercom, email and short video calls. Investigate thoroughly, keep people informed and follow through.

- 
 Make technical problems actionable. Reproduce bugs and give engineers clear steps, relevant logs and customer impact. Help distinguish product issues from gaps in understanding or setup.

- 
 Make answers easier to find. Turn useful solutions into Help Centre articles, internal guidance and short walkthroughs.

- 
 Build the support function. Identify what’s holding the team back and own improvements—from how we measure quality and prioritise work to the systems, playbooks and automations we use. Test new approaches, see whether they work and help the whole team improve.

- 
 Bring customer insight into the business. Help Product understand where users struggle, and work with Implementation and Customer Success when an issue needs broader attention.

 Success means customers get accurate answers quickly, issues reach a clear resolution, and the team gets better at preventing or handling the next one.

 What you’ll bring

- 
 Practical problem-solving. Evidence of getting to the bottom of unfamiliar problems, testing possible explanations and finding a workable solution.

- 
 Clear, empathetic communication. The ability to explain a complicated issue simply, adapt to different levels of technical confidence and build trust with frustrated customers.

- 
 High agency and drive. Examples of improving a process or building something useful—and seeing it through.

- 
 Reliability under pressure. Good judgement about urgency, careful follow-through and the ability to manage several conversations without losing track.

- 
 Curiosity about how products work. An appetite for learning Anima in depth and working closely with engineers to resolve problems.

 Relevant experience could come from customer support, technical operations, implementation or another role involving complex products and direct customer interaction. Experience with support platforms or process automation is useful; your judgement and results matter more than familiarity

 What we offer

 Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

- 
 Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

-

I quit medicine because I kept watching patients die needlessly, for avoidable reasons. In almost every case, the medical knowledge and clinicians were there. It was the system that failed: the way information moved, decisions got routed, and fragmented teams and data turned solvable problems into tragedy.

 I started Anima to change that.

 Our mission is human wellbeing, and we believe personalised medicine will transform it. Our founding insight is that getting there requires a system that learns continuously from care and its outcomes, optimising for human wellbeing. Building that learning engine is the opportunity at the heart of Anima.

 We're now in 1,000+ clinics across 5 product lines, serving more than 25% of the UK population. We are cash flow positive, growing fast, and have a tight crew of ~45 people who care deeply for each other and the mission. Everyone has real ownership and a voice in decisions.

 Multiple trillion-dollar companies will be built in healthcare over the next two decades. We intend to be one of them. 

 If you want to work on problems where the stakes are high, you belong at Anima. Your work here will save lives.

 -- Shun

 £65k–£90k base, plus equity 
 UK remote, UK working hours, with occasional UK customer visits 

 The role

 Help GP practices make a confident start with Anima.

 Last quarter, we onboarded 131 practices. We’re building a dedicated Implementation team to support that growth, and you’ll be one of its first members.

 You’ll own each implementation from kick-off through go-live and early support, helping practice teams build the skills and confidence to use Anima independently. You’ll also help shape how we implement: improving workflows, developing training and building a playbook that works across hundreds of practices.

 What you’ll do

- 
 Own implementations from start to finish. Coordinate kick-off, configuration and go-live, aiming to get most practices live within their first week.

- 
 Make Anima work for each practice. Understand how their team operates and configure workflows around their needs.

- 
 Teach people to use it confidently. Run clear, practical training for clinicians and practice teams, adapting your approach to different levels of technical confidence.

- 
 Build confidence beyond go-live. Develop practice super users, provide 1–2 weeks of hypercare and hand over cleanly to Support and Customer Success.

- 
 Make great implementation repeatable. Create reusable training and group webinars. Use feedback from customers, Support and CS to solve recurring problems at their source.

 What you’ll bring

- 
 SaaS experience. You’ve worked directly with customers on a SaaS product in onboarding, implementation or training.

- 
 Strong teaching and communication skills. You can make something unfamiliar feel manageable and check that people can put it into practice.

- 
 Patience and adaptability. You respond thoughtfully when someone is struggling or their priorities change.

- 
 Practical problem-solving. You learn products quickly and can work out why a workflow isn’t delivering the intended result.

- 
 Ownership and organisation. You can keep several implementations moving while making the next steps clear to everyone involved.

 Healthcare experience isn’t required—we’ll help you learn primary care. Experience creating training videos, guides or webinars would be useful.

 What we offer

 Anima should be where you do your life’s best work. We support that with:

- 
 Time off: 25 days’ annual leave plus 8 UK public holidays, with flexible additional time off.

- 
 Health cover: private medical, dental, vision and mental health insurance.

- 
 Parental leave: 12 weeks’ maternity leave at full pay, rising to 24 weeks after two years; 4 weeks’ paternity leave at full pay.

- 
 Pension: 4% employer contributions, with salary sacrifice and 100% of the employer National Insurance savings passed on to you.

- 
 Learning: £1,000 annual budget for your development.

- 
 Fitness: gym subscription matching up to £50 per month.

- 
 Equipment: a high-spec MacBook and a home office budget.

- 
 Time together: two full-team off-sites each year, previous destinations include Mykonos and Mexico.

- 
 Farringdon office: a beautiful new London HQ, with most of the team together at least twice a week.

 Everyone is welcome at Anima. We strongly believe in building a diverse and inclusive team. If you’re excited by our mission and believe you could do this work well, we’d love to hear from you, even if your experience doesn’t match every point above. If adjustments would help you participate fully in the interview process, please let us know.

Disclaimer: Stay safe from recruitment scams 
We only hire through , using TestGorilla assessments, video interviews and reference checks. We may contact you first on LinkedIn, but after that we only email from Teamtailor (@ / ) or @ addresses.
We will never ask you for money, interview you on Telegram or WhatsApp, or ask you to install software, connect a wallet or run code.
Not sure if a message is really from us? Ask us through our LinkedIn page before you reply.
 You know Bitrefill , and you’ve probably watched a search result or an app listing turn into revenue. You get that search no longer means just Google: people ask Claude and ChatGPT, and agents shop on their behalf. You want to own how 1M+ customers across 180+ countries find us. If that’s you, hit the apply button and let’s talk.

If you need more info to decide, keep reading. We kept the corporate fluff out, so it won't take long.

 About the role Organic discovery is changing fast. Programmatic SEO still matters, and so do the app stores. Now there’s a third channel: AI answer engines and AI agents that research, compare, and buy without ever opening a browser tab. We want Bitrefill to be the default answer in all three.
 You’ll have real freedom here. You choose where to build pages at scale, which experiments to run, and how to make us readable for machines. You’ll work closely with product, design, and engineering to get it shipped.
 What you'll do

- Own Bitrefill ’s organic growth strategy across search, app stores and AI

- Build and scale programmatic SEO: find the page types worth generating, then ship, measure and iterate

- Optimize our iOS and Android app listings with product and design: keywords, screenshots, store tests

- Make Bitrefill show up in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews, and whatever comes next)

- Make Bitrefill easy for AI agents to find and buy from: structured product data, machine-readable pages, and our agentic commerce work

- Write and shape content, and get your hands dirty in the front end when it’s faster than waiting on a ticket

- Track what’s working, kill what isn’t, and share findings with the team

 What we're looking for

- Be based in a timezone that aligns with Europe or the Americas

- 5+ years in growth, SEO, or performance marketing, with a track record of moving organic numbers

- Deep, hands-on programmatic and technical SEO experience. You’ve built pages at scale, not just audited them

- You’ve done hands-on GEO / AI visibility work and can show what it changed;

- AI is part of how you work (Claude, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Cursor, or similar). This is non-negotiable for us

- Comfortable with front-end basics. Some React is great, and vibecoding the rest is fine

- Strong writer with a good eye for design

- Data-driven. You read Search Console and analytics like a P&L

- Self-driven. You spot the opportunity and push it forward instead of waiting for a roadmap

 Bonus points

- Real ASO experience on iOS and Android

- Experience with structured data, llms.txt, or agent-facing APIs and MCP

- Crypto-native. You use it, and nobody needs to explain Bitcoin to you

- Experience in e-commerce or marketplace SEO with large catalogs

- Design chops in Figma for store assets and landing pages

 Why Bitrefill 

 We've been quietly right about something since 2014: internet money should just work. Fully remote since day one. Team across 30+ countries. Get paid in crypto if you want. No bullshit meetings. Twice a year, we meet up to build together in person. The rest of the time: work hard, get shit done.

Hello! 

 I’m Allie, Head of Support at Ashby . I’m excited to share that we’re hiring a Product Support Engineer in EMEA 🎉 

 We’re expanding our global Support team to provide 24/7 coverage across time zones. You’ll join a global team while establishing the technical Support Engineering presence in EMEA, with the ownership and visibility that come from being one of the first Support Engineers across European time zones. We staff across regions rather than relying on on-call rotations; we’ll discuss the specific schedule for this opening during the process.

 We’re hiring for both Product Support Specialist and Product Support Engineer roles. 

- 
 Support Specialist owns cases and customer communication end-to-end. Troubleshoots complex issues by navigating internal tooling — audit logs, user experience testing, and API testing — to help customers reach successful outcomes.

- 
 Support Engineering serves as the escalation point between Support Specialists and Product Engineering. Owns integrations, supports data mapping and data migrations for customers, and resolves escalated tickets that don't require product code changes.

 Support Engineering is the technical layer between frontline Support and Engineering. You’ll take on complex issues involving integrations, APIs, permissions, data, reporting, migrations, and workflows—using application behavior, logs, databases, and customer context to determine whether an issue can be resolved through Support or represents a product defect.

You’ll also identify recurring issues, improve documentation and enablement, and partner with Product and Engineering on improvements.  Identify recurring problems and turn them into documentation, enablement, tooling, process improvements, or product feedback.

- 
 Establish EMEA coverage, handoff, and operating practices across European time zones while bringing regional customer patterns to the global Support Engineering team.

- 
 Track and improve the outcomes that matter: resolution speed, escalation quality, fewer avoidable Engineering escalations, frontline self-sufficiency, reduced customer effort, and customer confidence.

 You should apply if: 

- 
 You’ve worked in a hands-on, customer-centric technical role where you independently investigate ambiguous issues involving APIs, integrations, logs, data, and application behavior.

- 
 You’re comfortable moving between customer conversations, APIs, logs, databases, product behavior, and code-level context to find root causes.

- 
 You can distinguish a configuration, data, documentation, or enablement issue from a true product defect—and explain your reasoning clearly.

- 
 You write precise investigations that others can quickly understand and act on, and communicate thoughtfully with technical and non-technical audiences across time zones.

- 
 You naturally look beyond the immediate ticket and improve the systems around it through documentation, enablement, tooling, or process design.

- 
 You want to be an early technical owner for EMEA and are energized by building regional structure within a global team.

 You should not apply if: 

- 
 You’re looking primarily for a high-volume support role centered on predefined troubleshooting steps, rather than open-ended technical investigation and ownership.

- 
 Most of your experience is in internal IT, help desk, endpoint, hardware, network, infrastructure, cloud operations, systems administration, infrastructure maintenance, or service deplo

 Schedule and run calls with customers who are blocked during self-onboarding and have escalated via chat or email.

 Comfort working across different channels (live chat, email, calls) and managing your own queue.

-

- 
 You get satisfaction from turning a stuck customer into a happy one.

 You like spotting patterns, asking why something keeps going wrong, and doing something about it.

- 
 You are organised and enjoy owning a caseload from start to finish.

- 
 This role is not a good fit for you if:

 You prefer to work without regular contact with customers.

 You find it hard to switch between many open cases and channels in a single day.

 How you'll develop in this role

 Build deep knowledge of Pleo's product and the most common onboarding blockers, so you can resolve cases faster.

 Take ownership of your own caseload and proactive outreach to stalled accounts.

About Supabase

 Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

 About the Role

 We are hiring a AI Platform Engineer to build the execution layer for Supabase's internal AI systems.

 Supabase is building an AI-native internal operating system: a common way of working across the company where AI carries a meaningful share of the operational load rather than sitting alongside it as an assistant. We are standing up a new central team to build those systems, enable the teams, and embed AI operations throughout the organization. You are the engineer on that team.

 The execution layer is yours. You will build the platform that actually runs agents: an event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime, durable state so work survives a restart, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and full logging of every prompt, tool call and decision so any run can be reconstructed. You will build the evaluation layer that makes any of it trustworthy, because an agent that cannot be measured cannot be trusted with anything beyond reading. And you will build the agents themselves, across everything from executive reporting down to a layer of agents that watch the platform and improve it.

 This is a governance-heavy environment by design, and that is the interesting part of the problem. Agents are risk-tiered from read-only internal data through to external-facing output, with review depth, evaluation requirements and human approval scaling by tier. Some capabilities are permanently off limits: an agent may read and report, it may carry a human-authored update into a system of record once a human consents, and it may initiate contact within a strict budget, but it may never autonomously write a commitment (an owner, a due date, a status) into a shared work system. Your job is to make that structurally impossible rather than merely forbidden.

 You will be the only engineer on this platform. You will close open architecture decisions yourself, own the infrastructure end to end, and instrument the system so it reports its own return.

 What You'll Be Responsible For

 In this role, you'll:

- 
 Ship the agent platform to production. An event-triggered queue, a headless model-agnostic runtime (choosing the runtime is an open decision you will close), durable state that survives a failed run, a human review gate, atomic rollback, and complete run logging in the warehouse.

- 
 Own the evaluation layer, and switch on the gate that depends on it. Golden suites with behavioral assertions rather than intuition, judge criteria with a written rubric, safety cases that must pass on every run, and a CI gate that blocks a regression from merging. This is the precondition for every agent that does anything beyond read internal data.

- 
 Build and register the agent portfolio. Reporting, drafting, linting, triage and question-answering agents across the executive, team-lead and individual-contributor layers, plus a meta layer that observes the platform and improves it.

- 
 Enforce governance in code. Risk tiers the pipeline actually enforces, least-privilege credentials per agent, tool-permission gates, a decision audit log, and autonomy classes where the dangerous class has no code path rather than a warning label. Nothing runs without a registered owner, tier, tool grant and human gate.

- 
 Design how the system contacts people. A hard interruption budget per person, message bundling instead of a stream of pings, and a structure that gives something useful before it asks for anything. Adoption depends on this more than on any other single design choice.

- 
 Own the platform tooling. The compiler and validator, inventory integrity, and the paths that distribute context and capabilities into the repositories and chat surfaces where work happens.

- 
 Compute the operating measures from production data. A pipeline from raw system activity through to a computed maturity grade per team, defensible enough that a team can dispute the result and be answered with the query rather than an opinion.

- 
 Instrument the platform's own return. A ledger that logs the work each agent absorbs and computes the monthly figure, so the value of the system is a measurement rather than a claim.

 How You'll Think

 Recursive Thinking

 You build the generator, not the artifact. When you need thirty agents, you do not write thirty agents; you build the inventory, the compiler and the distribution path that makes the thirty-first cost an afternoon, then a meta layer whose job is to watch the platform, find its drift and file the fix.

 The evaluation layer is the same move applied to trust. You are not checking whether one agent is correct today. You are building the machine that decides whether every future agent is allowed to ship, which

About Proper 

 Proper is an AI-first accounting service built for property managers and real estate operators. We combine automation, our own technology and a global team of accounting experts to run financial operations that are faster and more accurate than what the industry has settled for.

 We are 480 people across the US, Colombia and Mexico, serving 175 property management and real estate clients. We are a San Francisco based company and most of our accounting organisation is in Latin America.

 The role 

 You will run a pod: roughly 20 client accounts, 4 to 6 direct reports, and the 20 or so people who sit under them. Your direct reports are Senior Accountants and Principal Accountants, and each of them leads a small team and owns a set of clients.

 You are accountable for three things. Whether those clients stay. Whether the work reaching them is right. Whether the pod makes money.

 What makes this job different from most accounting management roles is where you sit. You are not the client's day-to-day contact, and you are not the last person to review every deliverable. Your Senior Accountants do that work and report to you on it. Your job is to know independently whether their picture is accurate, and to coach what you find. That means opening the books yourself, listening to recorded client calls, and forming your own view of an account rather than accepting a status update. If that sounds like less control than you are used to, it is actually more responsibility, and it is the part of the role we care most about.

 Key Responsibilities

- Knowing the truth about every account. Run health-check style reviews on client books, looking for discrepancies and for what they say about how the accounting has actually been done. Review our client health dashboard and act on what it surfaces. Spot check financials and client communications. Track error rates. Stay close to escalations and confirm they get resolved. 

- Coaching your team. This is the biggest part of the week. You will coach Senior and Principal Accountants on two things at once: running their own teams, and running their clients well. That includes reviewing recorded client calls and giving feedback specific enough to change what happens on the next one. 

- Client relationships and value. You check in on accounts on a regular cadence, and you take escalations that need someone more senior. You make sure we are delivering everything the client contracted for, and that our work is not quietly being absorbed back by the client's own team. 

- Quality and process. Individual errors get fixed by the team. Your job is to notice when a pattern of errors means something upstream has to change, and then change it. You will drive documentation and standardisation of client processes, and you will be the front line for rolling out new processes and automation with our Operations, Product and Engineering teams, including making sure the feedback from your team actually reaches them.

- The economics. You work with Finance and Workforce Management on capacity, cost to serve and gross margin per client, and you connect those numbers back to how your own pod is staffed and run.

 Qualifications & Required Skills

- At least two years managing senior individual contributors or managers, meaning people who had their own reports or owned their own client relationships. Managing a team of processors is not the same job.

- You have personally owned external client relationships. Clients you can name, where you were the person they emailed.

- Working knowledge of US GAAP including financial statement presentation. Enough to read a balance sheet, find something that does not tie, and challenge a senior accountant on it.

- Advanced English. You will be on calls with US property owners.

- Based in Mexico, with enough working-hours overlap to join US business-hours calls.

- One process improvement you ran end to end, where you can tell us the number before and the number after.

- A degree in accounting or demonstrated equivalent knowledge.

 Compensation

 Additional Information

In your first year, you’ll be expected to build strong, consultative relationships, increase product adoption and customer satisfaction within your accounts, and become the go-to liaison for questions, escalations, and roadmap conversations.

- Partner with customers to translate pre-sales command plans into clear, actionable objectives tied to their desired business outcomes.

- Guide customers on how to best use the GitLab platform, applying DevSecOps, CI/CD, and Git best practices across common use cases.

- Lead customers through their adoption journey, from onboarding and enablement to ongoing utilization and maturity of the platform.

- Own a portfolio of customers, focusing on driving product adoption, retention, expansion, and overall satisfaction.

- Act as the primary GitLab liaison for your accounts, coordinating with Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services on questions, issues, roadmaps, and escalations.

- Build and maintain Customer Success Plans with assigned customers, defining critical goals and key performance indicators, and track progress against those goals.

- Program manage account escalations, ensuring timely coordination, communication, and resolution across GitLab teams and customer stakeholders.

- Stay current on GitLab releases and new features, and proactively provide insights and recommendations on how customers can use them to achieve their objectives.

- Identify and recommend training and services opportunities that support customer enablement and long-term success.

 What you’ll bring

- Proven experience in customer success, post-sales, or professional services roles with a focus on driving adoption, retention, and measurable business outcomes.

- Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and the software development lifecycle, including continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices.

- Ability to act as a trusted advisor to technical and business stakeholders, partnering with customers to define, prioritize, and achieve their desired outcomes.

- Strong communication skills, including clear written and verbal communication, effective presentations, and the ability to explain technical topics to varied audiences.

- Demonstrated project management capabilities, including organizing work, managing escalations, and coordinating across internal teams such as Support, Product Management, Sales, and Services.

- Analytical and problem-solving skills to interpret customer data, identify risks or opportunities, and recommend act

All candidates from LATAM are welcome to apply!!! 
 About Us
 HireHawk connects talented professionals with growing international businesses, creating opportunities to work remotely with ambitious teams.
 We're recruiting on behalf of an innovative, sustainability-focused consumer brand with a strong direct-to-consumer presence in the UK and US. The business is rethinking everyday products through better design, sustainability, and an exceptional online shopping experience.
 About the Role
 We're looking for a E-commerce Operations Manager to take ownership of day-to-day website operations across the UK and US markets.
 You'll manage promotions, product launches, storefront updates, quality assurance, and third-party Shopify apps to deliver a reliable, seamless customer experience.
 This role goes beyond website maintenance. You'll use Claude, Shopify Sidekick, and Shopify Flow to automate repetitive processes, reduce manual work, and create scalable operating routines.
 As your automation efforts free up capacity, you'll collaborate with the Growth team on conversion optimization, A/B testing, and customer journey improvements.
 You'll report to the Head of Growth and collaborate closely with the Lead Developer, Growth Manager, CRM & Retention, Creative, and Customer Service teams.
 Responsibilities

- Own the monthly Shopify promotion cycle across UK and US markets, ensuring accurate pricing, discounts, scheduling, and promotional changes.

- Deliver seamless product launches by managing SKUs, variants, imagery, descriptions, collections, preorders, and product drops.

- Build and maintain campaign landing pages using existing Shopify components and AI-powered page-building tools.

- Protect the customer experience through thorough QA testing across product pages, navigation, subscriptions, carts, and checkout on desktop and mobile.

- Manage Shopify storefront applications, including Skio, AfterSell, and Fairing, while tracking application ownership, costs, and renewals.

- Automate promotions, product setup, and pre-launch QA workflows using Claude, Shopify Flow, Shopify Sidekick, and scheduled checks.

- Create proactive monitoring routines to identify pricing inconsistencies, product availability issues, and other storefront errors before they affect customers.

- Document operational processes and develop reusable workflows that reduce manual workload and improve team efficiency.

- Support A/B testing initiatives by launching experiments, monitoring results, and documenting findings alongside the Growth team.

- Analyze customer behavior using GA4, Microsoft Clarity, and Fairing to identify friction points and recommend conversion improvements.

 Requirements

 Must-Have: 

- At least 3 years of hands-on Shopify administration experience within a direct-to-consumer (DTC) e-commerce brand. 

- Experience managing Shopify products, pricing, discounts, Markets, promotions, and storefront applications across multiple markets or currencies. 

- Strong understanding of Shopify's ecosystem, including themes, apps, checkout processes, and subscription functionality. Coding experience is not required. 

- Practical experience using AI tools to automate daily workflows, including at least one automation or routine you have personally built and can demonstrate. 

- Strong quality assurance skills, with a structured approach to testing, identifying edge cases, documenting issues, and preventing recurring errors. 

- Working knowledge of Klaviyo and Gorgias, plus excellent written and spoken English for communicating with UK and US teams and customers. 

- Availability to work Monday to Friday, 9 AM–5 PM UK time, with some flexibility around start and finish times. 

 Nice to Have: 

- Experience supporting A/B testing and conversion rate optimization initiatives. 

- Familiarity with Skio or other subscription platforms, AfterSell, and Fairing. 

- Experience building automated workflows using Shopify Flow, n8n, Zapier, or Claude skills and connectors. 

- Familiarity with Claude Code or Cursor for small website or landing page adjustments. 

- Experience interpreting customer behavior data using GA4, Microsoft Clarity, or similar analytics tools.

Hi there! Do not apply until you have read this entire job posting. We can tell when someone hasn't, and those applications will not be considered.
 About Us
 Content Mindset is a small but growing video editing agency. We partner with social media teams to handle 100% of their video editing needs. You will be working alongside a team of editors, and you'll be getting edits that push you to grow as an editor.
 We are hiring a freelance short-form video editor dedicated to one of our clients: a software company that markets to e-commerce brands. The client posts 3 times per week, and you will be the editor behind those videos.
 The Style
 The main inspiration for this role is Rourke's Instagram page: 
 Study it before you apply. Think cinematic AI-generated scenes, bold animated text, fast pacing, and motion graphics that keep every second visually interesting. We want videos that feel like they were made by someone who lives on the internet and genuinely loves what AI can do for video.
 What You'll Be Doing

- Editing 3 short-form vertical videos per week for our client

- Using AI tools to generate animations, visuals, and scenes that bring each script to life

- Building motion graphics: animated text, popups, callouts, and UI highlights

- Sourcing B-roll, including screen recording B-roll from e-commerce brand websites (storefronts, product pages, checkout flows)

- Adding and proofreading captions on every video

- Working with our team on review notes and revisions

 Pay
 This is a freelance role paid per video, at $50 USD per video . At 3 videos per week, that's $150 USD per week. We also give our editors a $10 weekly bonus, just for being a part of the team. Payment is always sent Friday evening PST. We also host our team meetings Friday evening PST.
 Requirements

- Adobe Premiere Pro 2026 (non-negotiable)

- Very comfortable using AI tools for video. You use AI image and video generators (Runway, Kling, Higgsfield, Luma, Veo, or similar) to create animations and scenes, and you keep up with new tools as they come out

- Strong motion graphics skills

- Comfortable sourcing B-roll and recording clean, high-quality screen recordings of websites (smooth scrolling, clean cursor movement, high resolution)

- Internet-native. You understand short-form, trends, retention, and what makes someone stop scrolling

- Excited about AI and always trying to get better as an editor. You take feedback well and actively look for ways to level up

- Very communicative and enjoys being part of a team

- Reliable turnaround. The client posts 3 times per week, so hitting deadlines matters

- 
 Fluent / Almost Fluent English speaker

- Premiere captioning isn't the best with grammar, you'd be expected to correct this on your own

- Comfortable with large file sizes (50+ GB in some cases)

- Open to working with us long term

 Nice to have: experience editing for tech, software, or e-commerce brands.
 How to Apply
 The only way to apply is through our application form. Have 2 to 3 examples of your work ready, ideally videos where you used AI-generated visuals or motion graphics.
 APPLY HERE: 
 If you do not fill out the form, we will not consider your application. We will reach out to people who are a good fit via email.

Ververica is the original creator of Apache Flink® and remains a core contributor to it. Flink is the leading open-source engine for stream and batch processing. It runs mission-critical workloads at Netflix, Alibaba, Amazon and Uber, as well as at banks, telcos and global enterprises.

We build Ververica Unified Streaming Data Platform, an enterprise-grade platform for real-time data on top of Flink. Backed by one of the world's largest tech companies, we combine open-source innovation with long-term stability.

 WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS 
Our customers run real-time pipelines that cannot stop: fraud detection, payments, telemetry, recommendations. When something breaks, you are the engineer who gets it running again.

As a Technical Support Engineer , you will solve real production problems on Kubernetes, in the cloud and inside Flink itself. You will work side by side with the engineers who build Flink, so every hard ticket is a chance to learn how a distributed system works under the hood.

This role suits someone who enjoys a good puzzle, likes helping people and wants to grow into a stream processing expert. WHAT YOU BRING

- 2+ years in technical support or a similar hands-on role, ideally with cloud-based products.

- Solid knowledge of at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure or Google Cloud).

- Practical experience with containers and Kubernetes. Our product runs on Kubernetes, so this matters.

- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills. You enjoy finding out why something fails.

- Clear written and spoken English, and the patience to explain technical ideas to any audience.

- A customer-first mindset and the ability to stay calm when a customer is under pressure.

- Ability to work independently and as part of a distributed team.

- Curiosity and a drive to keep learning.

- A degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

 NICE TO HAVE 

No one ticks every box. If you have some of these, tell us. 

- Experience with stream processing, Apache Flink or Apache Kafka.

- Scripting or programming skills in Shell, Python, Java or SQL.

- Experience with Terraform or other infrastructure-as-code tools.

- Experience with cloud monitoring and observability tools.

- Cloud certifications such as AWS Certified Solutions Architect or Azure Administrator.

 LOCATION AND WORKING HOURS 

This is a remote role for someone based between UTC-4 and UTC-7. That covers US and Canadian Eastern, Central, Mountain and Pacific time, plus Latin American countries in the same range.

- Your core hours follow customers' business day in the Americas.

- You will work closely with our EMEA support team to give customers follow-the-sun coverage.

 WHAT YOU WILL DO

- Be the first technical point of contact for customers using Ververica Unified Streaming Data Platform.

- Diagnose and fix issues across the stack, from Kubernetes and cloud infrastructure to Flink jobs, connectors and SQL.

- Reproduce tricky problems, dig through logs and metrics, and find the root cause.

- Escalate to Engineering and Product with clear, well-documented cases, and help shape fixes and product improvements.

- Explain solutions and best practices clearly to engineers and non-technical stakeholders alike.

- Keep accurate records of cases and resolutions in our ticketing system.

- Turn what you learn into knowledge base articles, tutorials and runbooks that help customers and teammates.

- Keep sharpening your skills in cloud technologies and stream processing, and share them with the team.

 WHAT WE OFFER

- Competitive compensation: salary, equity and performance bonus

- Remote-first culture with flexible hours

- Direct access to Flink core developers and a global open-source community

- A clear path to grow into senior support, Technical Account Manager or engineering roles

- Generous vacation, personal leave and wellness benefits

At Ververica, we believe innovation starts with diverse perspectives. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds. If you are passionate about helping customers succeed with real-time data, we would love to hear from you.

 Apache Flink® is a trademark of the Apache Software Foundation. Originally posted on Himalayas

Job Title: Senior Integrations Engineer 
 Location Preference: 100% remote in LATAM with preference in Chile working EST Time Zone 
 Duration: 1-Year Assignment with possibility of extension
 NTT DATA is a team of more than 139,000 diverse professionals operating in more than 50 countries worldwide. Our sectors of activity include telecommunications, finance, industry, utilities, energy, public administration, and health.
 Our mission? Offer technological solutions, business, strategy, development, and application maintenance while being a benchmark in consulting. Thanks to the collaboration between teams, the human quality of our people, and the fact that we do not conform to what is established, we always seek innovation that brings us closer to the future.
 Our essence has led us to the forefront of technology, breaking paradigms and providing solutions that truly respond to each client's needs. Our talent has led us to be one of the top six technology companies in the world.
 Because #Greattech, needs #GreatPeople, like you
 NTT Data seeks high-achieving team players who quickly adapt to new challenges and entrepreneurial ventures. We are looking for a Senior Integrations Engineer to work with our global client for a fully remote opportunity in LATAM working EST hours. 
 Position Summary 
 Data integration engineer specialized in designing, developing, and operating enterprise data pipelines on ETL tools; Informatica IDMC (Intelligent Data Management Cloud / IICS) as the primary platform, with strong capabilities in feeding the Databricks Lakehouse. Able to work across cloud-agnostic environments (Azure, AWS, GCP) and to apply AI-assisted development with CLAIRE GPT and CLAIRE Copilot to accelerate the build cycle and reduce time-to-delivery.
 Key Responsibilities 

- Design and implement ingestion, transformation, and distribution pipelines with CDI and Cloud Mass Ingestion.

- Build and optimize ingestion and ELT into the Databricks Lakehouse using IDMC for Databricks and Delta Lake patterns.

- Migrate PowerCenter workloads to IDMC using structured methodology and internal accelerators.

- Operate and maintain integration infrastructure (Secure Agents, runtimes) on Azure and AWS under SLA standards.

- Apply CLAIRE GPT/Copilot to optimize the mapping development cycle and reduce delivery time.

 Requirements 
 Technical Skills: 

- 
 Informatica IDMC · Integration Core 

- Cloud Data Integration (CDI): Mapping Designer, SQL ELT with pushdown optimization (full/source/target), Taskflows, mapping partitioning, Dynamic Mappings, parameterization, file listeners, intelligent structure models (CLAIRE-powered), and performance tuning.

- Cloud Mass Ingestion (CMI): batch and near-real-time ingestion from heterogeneous sources across its variants: Mass Ingestion Databases (CDC), Files, Applications, and Streaming.

- Cloud Application Integration (CAI): Process Designer, service connectors, guides, and business processes; API and microservices integration.

- PowerCenter to IDMC: migration and modernization of on-premises pipelines using structured methodology, CDI-PC, and migration accelerators.

- Platform operations: administration of Secure Agents and runtime environments (Secure Agent Groups), monitoring, and SLA management.

 Databricks Integration 

- IDMC for Databricks: ingestion and ELT into the Databricks Lakehouse with CDI and Cloud Mass Ingestion, Delta Lake load patterns, and SQL ELT pushdown to Databricks SQL.

- Connectivity through the Databricks connector (Partner Connect), Unity Catalog awareness, and parameterized job orchestration.

 AI-Assisted Development (CLAIRE) 

- CLAIRE GPT / CLAIRE Copilot: assisted generation of mappings, debugging of transformations, and automatic pipeline documentation through natural language within IDMC.

- Awareness of the new agentic capabilities ( CLAIRE Agents , Fall 2025 release) for headless ingestion and transformation flows.

 Platform FinOps 

- Understanding of the IPU (Informatica Processing Units) consumption model and per-service cost optimization.

 Cloud-Agnostic (Complementary) 

- Azure: Azure Data Factory (ADF), Data Lake Storage Gen2, Key Vault, Azure Databricks.

- AWS: Glue, S3, Step Functions, Redshift, Athena, EventBridge.

- GCP (desirable): BigQuery, Cloud Composer.

- IaC & CI/CD for pipelines: Terraform, CloudFormation; GitHub/Bitbucket, Jenkins.

 Databases & Platforms 

- Advanced SQL (Oracle, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Redshift, Databricks SQL).

- NoSQL (MongoDB, DynamoDB; desirable).

- Data Warehouse, Data Lake, and Lakehouse architecture patterns.

 Certifications: 

- Informatica Cloud Data Integration Developer, Professional Certification (ICP) (core to the role).

- Informatica Cloud Application Integration Developer, Professional Certification (desirable).

- Informatica IDMC Foundation / Data Engineering Foundation.

- Databricks Certified Data Engineer Associate (desirable).

- Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Engineer As
